description:
Creating an extensive wild meadow flower green roof on what is now a flat roof. 
This has environmental benefits including; sustainable drainage (aiming to reduce runoff by 55-60%), increased biodiversity, reduced urban heat and improved water and air quality. It is also energy saving (thermal mass) reducing heating and cooling costs.
The roof is 10x15m in size with two skylights. The roof can be accessed by one of the skylights for tri-annual maintenance and more intensive watering required during the initial establishment phase. Guardrails will be required to provide collective protection that complies to “Work at Height” regulations. 
Although a structural survey has not yet been completed, it is likely that the present concrete roof will require reinforcement to support the extra load. 
The plan is for a 100-150mm deep substrate to cover the roof apart from the pebble firebreaks running around the perimeter and skylights. The meadow will be 100m2.
The site is the roof of a 3-storey ex-council terrace house. Bride Street is a very quiet road with a barrier to stop through traffic. It is likely that a crane will be required to lift material to roof level. We have excellent relationships with our neighbours and friends on Bride Street and will communicate clearly to them to do what we can to keep disruption to a minimum.
Our neighbours are very supportive of the plan and are happy to write letters of support, if required.
